# What to build vs. what to build in 8 hours

The full vision is too big for 8 hours: engine plugins for Unity and Unreal, a cloud fleet of agents, billing and a marketplace. The hackathon version should prove one claim end to end: AI agents find bugs in a game overnight, and Cline helps fix them.

## The 8-hour MVP

A small game with planted bugs, a swarm of bots that play it, an automatic bug report for each failure, and a Cline-assisted fix.

1. Game under test: a tiny headless Python grid game (keys, doors, coins, enemies) with a seed for deterministic replay. Plant 4 bugs on purpose so the demo is reliable:
- A softlock: a player who drops the key in a pit can't finish.
- A hole in the map: one tile lets you walk through a wall.
- An economy exploit: a coin duplication loop.
- A crash on one specific input sequence.
2. Agent swarm: run many bots in parallel with different behaviors (random walker, goal-seeker, chaos tester that spams odd inputs).
3. Detectors: simple rules, no ML needed.
- Crash: an exception is thrown.
- Softlock: no progress for N steps.
- Hole in the map: the player is inside a wall or outside the map.
- Exploit: the score or inventory jumps impossibly.
4. Bug reports: each bug gets the seed, the action sequence to reproduce it, and a replay GIF. Duplicates are merged by signature.
5. LLM triage: send each report to Claude to write a title, severity and suspected cause.
6. Dashboard: a Streamlit page showing runs, bugs found and a replay viewer.
7. Cline moment: give Cline a bug report. It reads the code, proposes a fix, you approve it, the swarm reruns and the bug is gone.

## What we will not build

- Real Unity or Unreal integration (say it's on the roadmap)
- Reinforcement learning (scripted and random bots are enough)
- Auth, billing, multi-tenant cloud, the marketplace
- Video capture from a real engine (GIF replay is enough)

## Hour-by-hour plan

| Time | Goal |
|---|---|
| 0:00–0:45 | Agree scope, set up repo, have Cline scaffold the game and plant the 4 bugs |
| 0:45–2:30 | Environment interface (reset, step, state), the three bot types, parallel runs |
| 2:30–4:00 | The four detectors, tested against the planted bugs |
| 4:00–5:30 | Repro files, GIF replays, dedupe, Claude triage |
| 5:30–6:30 | Streamlit dashboard |
| 6:30–7:15 | Cline fix demo: before and after rerun |
| 7:15–8:00 | Polish, rehearse, record a backup demo video, trim the slides |

## Suggested roles (3–4 people)

- Game and bugs: the game, planted bugs, replay renderer
- Agents and detectors: bots, swarm runner, detection rules
- AI and reports: Claude triage, dedupe, report format
- Demo and story: dashboard, Cline fix flow, slides, pitch

## Demo script (about 3 minutes)

1. State the problem in one line: QA can't keep up with game complexity.
2. Kick off the swarm live and show bugs appearing on the dashboard.
3. Open one bug: replay, repro steps, Claude's triage.
4. Show Cline reading the bug, proposing a fix, and you approving it.
5. Rerun the swarm and show that bug is gone.
6. Close on the business model: subscription plus usage-based pricing.

## Success metric

Report something you can verify live: "found all 4 planted bugs automatically, and one was fixed and re-verified." Don't claim numbers you haven't measured.

## Risks and fallbacks

- Detectors are flaky: hardcode the planted bugs' signatures first, then generalize if time allows.
- LLM call fails on stage: cache triage results beforehand.
- Cline fix goes sideways: pre-record one successful run as a backup.
- Running behind: cut in this order: GIF replay, then dedupe, then the dashboard. Keep the swarm, the detectors and the Cline fix.

### The game and the 4 planted bugs

12×10 ASCII grid: # wall, . floor, P start, K key, D locked door, C coin, G goal, ~ pit, plus one wall tile that is wrongly walkable. Actions UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT/USE/PICKUP/DROP/WAIT. reset(seed) seeds one random.Random used for enemy movement, so (seed, actions) fully determines a trajectory — that is what makes the repro file and the GIF trustworthy rather than decorative.

Each bug lives behind a BUG_FLAGS toggle with a greppable # BUG: comment, so the Cline fix is a small, legible diff:

| Bug | Mechanism | Detector | Signature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Softlock | DROP over a pit deletes the key from the world instead of placing it on the floor → door unreachable | progress signature unchanged for N=60 steps, goal not reached | (softlock, map_id) |
| Map hole | off-by-one when building the walkable set registers one wall tile as floor | MAP_RAW[pos] == "#" or out of bounds | (map_hole, x, y) |
| Economy exploit | collected set keyed by position *after* the move, so pickup → step away → step back duplicates a coin | coins > world.total_coins or score delta > MAX_LEGAL_GAIN | (exploit, kind) |
| Crash | [USE, DROP, USE] on the door tile → unguarded inventory.index("key") raises | any exception escaping step() | (crash, exc_type, file:line:func) |

Two details that matter for the demo being *honest*:
- Signatures include the exception site / tile coordinate, not the seed — so 40 bots hitting the same wall tile merge into one report instead of 40.
- On merge, keep the shortest repro action list. Shorter repros are far easier to show on stage.

### Swarm, triage, replay, dashboard

- Parallel: ProcessPoolExecutor, workers take (seed, bot_name, max_steps) and build the env internally (nothing unpicklable crosses the boundary); parent writes reports so there are no concurrent file writes. Sized so 200 episodes × 300 steps finish well under a minute — it has to run *live*.
- Triage: one Claude Messages call per signature asking for strict JSON {title, severity, suspected_cause, suggested_fix_area}, cached at artifacts/triage_cache/<signature>.json. Pre-warming that cache is your stage-failure fallback — on API error, load cache and show a "cached" badge.
- GIF: Pillow only, no imageio/matplotlib. Re-simulate from (seed, actions) rather than recording live, so it stays deterministic.
- Dashboard: KPI header (episodes, steps, bugs, unique signatures, verified-fixed) → auto-refreshing findings feed → bug detail with severity, triage, copyable seed + action string, st.image(gif), and a per-step ASCII trace table → "Verify fix" button.

### The integrity guard on the success metric

scripts/verify_fix.py must rerun the whole swarm and assert two things: the target signature has 0 occurrences, and the other three detectors still fire. Without the second assertion, "the bug is gone" could just mean a detector broke. That is what makes *"found all 4 planted bugs, fixed one, re-verified"* defensible when someone asks you live.

tests/test_planted_bugs.py pins a fixed seed + fixed action list per bug that must produce that detector's finding. Running it before you go on stage tells you the demo will work — this is the real mitigation for "detectors are flaky," and it costs about 20 minutes. The random swarm on top is showmanship; the pinned repros are the guarantee.

### Cut order refinement

Your order (GIF → dedupe → dashboard) is right, with one addition: if the GIF is cut, the dashboard still shows a frame slider over the recorded ASCII trace. That needs no new code, because the runner records render_state() per step anyway — so cutting the GIF costs you almost nothing visually.

1
+
# AI Game QA Swarm
2
+
3
+
An AI agent swarm that plays a small grid game, finds real bugs, writes
4
+
reproducible bug reports, triages them with Claude, and then proves a fix
5
+
worked — without a human writing a single test case.
6
+
7
+
Built as an 8-hour hackathon MVP. The core runtime has **zero hard
8
+
dependencies**: the game, agents, detectors, report store, swarm and CLI all
9
+
run on the Python standard library. Pillow, Streamlit and the Anthropic SDK
10
+
are optional and each one degrades gracefully when missing.
11
+
12
+
---
13
+
14
+
## The 60-second version
15
+
16
+
```bash
17
+
pip install -r requirements.txt
18
+
19
+
# 1. Prove the demo works before you trust it (finds all 4 planted bugs
20
+
# from fixed, verified seeds)
21
+
python scripts/seed_bugs.py
22
+
23
+
# 2. Let the swarm loose: 60 episodes, 3 bot types, 4 detectors
24
+
python -m gameqa.cli run --episodes 20 --triage
25
+
26
+
# 3. Look at what it found
27
+
python -m gameqa.cli list
28
+
python -m gameqa.cli show crash
29
+
30
+
# 4. Watch a bug happen, frame by frame
31
+
python -m gameqa.cli replay --seed 42 --actions "RIGHT,RIGHT,PICKUP"
32
+
33
+
# 5. Fix one bug (with Cline, or by hand), then prove it's fixed
34
+
python scripts/verify_fix.py --kind crash
35
+
36
+
# 6. Dashboard
37
+
streamlit run dashboard/app.py
38
+
```
39
+
40
+

41
+
42
+
## What it actually does
43
+
44
+
```
45
+
┌──────────────┐
46
+
seed ────────▶│ GridGame │ deterministic: (seed, actions) -> run
47
+
│ 4 planted │
48
+
│ bugs │
49
+
└──────┬───────┘
50
+
│ obs / reward / done / info
51
+
┌───────────────┼───────────────────┐
52
+
▼ ▼ ▼
53
+
random_walker goal_seeker chaos_tester
54
+
└───────────────┼───────────────────┘
55
+
│ every step is recorded
56
+
▼
57
+
┌───────────────────────────────────┐
58
+
│ 4 rule-based detectors │
59
+
│ crash / softlock / map_hole / │
60
+
│ exploit │
61
+
└───────────────┬───────────────────┘
62
+
│ Finding(kind, signature, detail)
63
+
▼
64
+
┌───────────────────────────────────┐
65
+
│ dedupe by signature -> BugReport │ repro = (seed, actions)
66
+
│ + replay GIF + Claude triage │
67
+
└───────────────┬───────────────────┘
68
+
▼
69
+
dashboard / cli / verify
70
+
```
71
+
72
+
### The four planted bugs
73
+
74
+
Each is gated behind a flag in `gameqa/game/bugs.py` and marked with a
75
+
`# BUG:` comment at its site in `gameqa/game/grid_game.py`, so a fix is a
76
+
small, legible diff.
77
+
78
+
| Bug | Kind | What's wrong | How it's caught |
79
+
|---|---|---|---|
80
+
| Key lost in pit | `softlock` | `DROP` on a pit destroys the key instead of refusing, so the door can never open | BFS reachability proof over the *intended* map |
81
+
| Walkable wall | `map_hole` | Off-by-one registers one wall tile as floor; the player walks through a pillar | Position checked against `MAP_RAW`, not the game's own walkable set |
82
+
| Coin duplication | `exploit` | The "already paid" guard is wiped on every move and coins are never marked taken | Hard arithmetic: `coins_collected > total_coins`, `score > max_legal_score` |
83
+
| Stale key flag | `crash` | `USE` trusts a flag `DROP` never clears, then indexes an empty inventory | Any exception escaping `step()` is a bug |
84
+
85
+
### Why the detectors are trustworthy
86
+
87
+
A detector that reads the game's own model of itself cannot notice the game
88
+
lying about that model — which is exactly what the map-hole bug does. So each
89
+
detector uses an **independent truth source**:
90
+
91
+
* **map_hole** compares against `MAP_RAW` (declared level data), never against
92
+
`env.walkable`.
93
+
* **softlock** is a real reachability proof (BFS over the intended map with the
94
+
door's true state), not a "the bot stood still for N steps" counter. A bot
95
+
wandering in circles is not a bug; a world state from which the goal is
96
+
provably unreachable is.
97
+
* **exploit** is pure arithmetic against constants derived from the level data.
98
+
* **crash** treats any escaping exception as a bug and signs it by
99
+
`ExceptionType|file:line:function`.
100
+
101
+
### Why the repros are trustworthy
102
+
103
+

## CLI reference

+
67
+
| Command | What it does |
68
+
|---|---|
69
+
| `run` | Run the swarm, merge findings into reports, render GIFs. `--triage` also runs Claude. `--disable crash exploit` simulates a fix. |
70
+
| `plant` | Search seeds for a verified repro of each planted bug. `--record` writes them into the store. Exits non-zero if any bug fails to reproduce. |
71
+
| `triage` | Triage stored reports. `--force` ignores the cache, `--offline` forces the heuristic. |
72
+
| `list` | Severity, occurrence count, fixed state and signature for every report. |
73
+
| `show <sig>` | Print one report's repro file (substring match works). |
74
+
| `replay` | Re-simulate `--seed` + `--actions`; print ASCII frames, or `--gif out.gif`. |
75
+
| `verify --kind K` | Prove `K` is gone **and** the other three are still detected. |

## The fix-and-verify flow
80
+
81
+
This is the part that makes the demo more than a bug-finding toy.
82
+
83
+
```bash
84
+
# BEFORE: 4 bugs, 4 kinds of finding
85
+
python -m gameqa.cli run --episodes 20
86
+
87
+
# FIX: ask Cline to fix one bug from its repro alone.
88
+
# "Fix the bug described in artifacts/repros/<crash-signature>.txt.
89
+
# The repro is deterministic: seed + action list. Do not touch the
90
+
# detectors or the tests. Mark your change with a comment."
91
+
# Cline sees the repro, the traceback, the detector detail and the map data --
92
+
# never the `# BUG:` comments -- so the fix has to be earned.
93
+
94
+
# AFTER: prove it
95
+
python scripts/verify_fix.py --kind crash
96
+
```
97
+
98
+
`verify` passes only when **all three** hold:
99
+
100
+
1. The target bug's pinned repro produces no finding across a 200-seed search.
101
+
2. Every *other* planted bug's pinned repro **still** fires.
102
+
3. A fresh swarm run finds 0 occurrences of the target kind while still
103
+
finding the other three kinds.
104
+
105
+
Condition 2 is the one that matters. Without it, "the crash no longer appears"
106
+
is worthless — a broken detector also produces zero findings. This is what
107
+
turns the success metric from *"the AI said it fixed it"* into *"the harness
108
+
proves the bug is gone and detection did not regress."*
109
+
110
+
`python scripts/verify_fix.py --simulate` runs the same verification for all
111
+
four bugs by flipping their flags off in turn, so you can prove the verify
112
+
harness itself works before relying on it live.

## Design notes and honest limitations
50
+
51
+
**Determinism is load-bearing.** Everything downstream — repro files, replay
52
+
GIFs, fix verification — depends on `(seed, actions)` reproducing a run
53
+
exactly. Two consequences worth knowing:
54
+
55
+
* Bot RNG seeds are derived from the bot *name* with a stable sum, not
56
+
Python's built-in `hash()`, which is salted per process and would silently
57
+
make worker processes disagree with the parent.
58
+
* Replay GIFs are re-simulated, not recorded. Slower, but they can never drift
59
+
from the repro they claim to illustrate.
60
+
61
+
**Scripted repros are machine-verified, not assumed.** Enemies patrol the
62
+
lower corridor and block movement like a wall, so a fixed action list can
63
+
desync on some seeds. `repros.find_seed()` therefore searches seeds and keeps
64
+
only one that actually reproduces the bug. Anything that claims a repro works
65
+
without running it is lying.
66
+
67
+
**Enemies block but do not kill.** They deal no damage and end nothing, which
68
+
keeps them out of the detectors' way. A damaging enemy would need its own
69
+
detector and its own notion of "legal", which was out of scope for 8 hours.
70
+
71
+
**One map, one level.** `MAP_RAW` is a single 12x10 level. The detectors are
72
+
map-agnostic (they read `MAP_RAW` and level constants), so a second level is a
73
+
data change rather than a detector change — but that is untested.
74
+
75
+
**Detectors are deliberately dumb.** Four hand-written rules with independent
76
+
truth sources. No ML, no tuning, no learned invariants. That is the point: on
77
+
stage you can read the rule that fired and agree with it in ten seconds. The
78
+
swarm supplies coverage; the detectors supply judgement.
79
+
80
+
**Triage is advisory.** Claude's title, severity and suspected cause are
81
+
recorded on the report and cached on disk. They never gate anything. The
82
+
`verify` flow is entirely deterministic and does not call the API, so the
83
+
success metric cannot depend on a model's opinion.
84
+
85
+
**Bots are simple on purpose.** A random walker, a greedy goal seeker and a
86
+
chaos tester find all four planted bugs within a few dozen episodes. A smarter
87
+
planner would find them faster but would make the demo less honest about how
88
+
much coverage cheap agents actually buy you.
89
+

- test_reachable_set_escapes_an_off_map_start — reachable_set seeds from adjacent walkable tiles; a truly walled-in tile still degenerates to {start}.

3. Caught and fixed a regression I introduced

The first run gave detectors 22/22 but planted-bugs 9/10 — test_swarm_finds_all_four_kinds missed crash. My to_pit phase was the culprit: it advanced at *planning* time, so once the pit DROP destroyed the key, to_key fell through to "wander" and returned [] forever. The gremlin could never play the door burst again, so the crash disappeared.

I replaced the phase machine with state-driven priorities — every branch decided from the current observation, so a discarded plan just re-decides:
1. fetch the key whenever obtainable;
2. drop it in a pit, re-routed until the DROP actually lands on a pit tile (_pit_done is set in act(), not in _plan() — the same lesson as the GoalSeeker probe), and attempted at most once so it can't loop pick-up/drop forever when the softlock bug is fixed;
3. always fall through to the door burst, which needs no key and so is still worth playing after the key is destroyed.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| tests/test_detectors.py | 22/22 |
| tests/test_planted_bugs.py | 10/10 |
| scripts/seed_bugs.py --record | all 4 pinned repros ok |
| scripts/verify_fix.py --simulate | OVERALL: PASS (all four kinds) |
| swarm, 15 ep/bot | 4 signatures, wins=15, crashes=15 |
| swarm, 40 ep/bot (120 total) | 4 signatures, wins=40/40, crashes=40 |

Final 120-episode run:
findings=137  unique signatures=4
  crash 40 | exploit 46 | map_hole 10 | softlock 41
  [critical] level cannot be completed: key_destroyed  x41  (softlock|level_01|key_destroyed)


The goal_unreachable false positive is gone entirely — the softlock signature is now the genuine key_destroyed, and there is no duplicate report for the map hole.

The strongest evidence is from verify_fix: with the softlock bug flipped off, the swarm reports 0 occurrences of 'softlock' in 24 episodes. A detector that merely went quiet would be indistinguishable from a broken one, so that script also confirms the other three kinds still fire in the same run — which they do.

## Two things to flag

- verify_fix.py --simulate was run scoped down to --search 40 --episodes 8 instead of the defaults (200/20). The full run kept exceeding the command window and getting killed before it finished, so I reduced the seed search to get a complete result. Worth re-running at defaults yourself before the stage demo; the reduced run is representative but not as thorough.
- The "attempt the pit drop once" rule is deliberate. With the softlock bug fixed, the key survives the drop, so re-fetching and re-dropping would loop indefinitely and starve the door burst. That's exactly the verify_fix softlock-disabled case, and it passes — crash/exploit/map_hole are all still found there.

I also removed the scratch files I'd accumulated during diagnosis (t*.log, compile.log, pkgs.log, diag.py). The project root is back to .env.example, .gitignore, README.md, requirements.txt. Note the directory is not a git repo, so none of these changes are under version control — you may want to git init before the demo if you want a rollback point.
